steps.prompt: Close your eyes for a moment. What does your kitchen sound and smell like in the morning?

cards.title: Your five senses
cards.body: Sight, sound, smell, taste and touch. Most writers only use sight. Adding the other senses pulls the reader right into the scene.

cards.title: Name it vs. describe it
cards.text: Instead of "a dog", try "a wet nose, a thumping tail, and muddy paw prints across the kitchen floor."
cards.note: You never said "dog", but the reader sees one, and even hears the tail.

cards.title: Which senses?
cards.prompt: Tap the four words that use sound, smell or touch.
cards.text: The bread crackled as Dad tore it open, and warm, buttery steam filled the kitchen.

cards.title: The secret: specific details
cards.body: "A red bike with a squeaky bell" beats "a bike". Specific details let readers picture things for themselves.

prompts: Which sense was hardest to write about? Why?
Read your description to someone. Could they guess what it was?
